origin.rerun: grep -n 'releasing %s and retrying once' src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py; journal ict-trader-live grep 'releasing' for an alpaca place_protective(<sym>) line, each one is a sibling TP released

what: Netted Alpaca symbol: second package's TP released to arm the first; needs a merged-OCO design. Alpaca nets per symbol, so when a re-arm OCO for one journal row is refused while a SIBLING row's standalone take-profit rests on the same reducing side (the shares are shared, 'insufficient qty available'), AlpacaClient.place_protective RELEASES (DELETEs) that sibling target and retries the OCO once (kept as documented, manager 2026-11-17 06:02Z). If the retry succeeds the sibling row is left with no take-profit: a TP-doctrine gap (the sibling's TP is lost to arm the first package's stop). #26611 restores the released target only when the retry is also refused. Needs a design that holds both packages' protection on one netted position (one merged OCO sized to the netted qty with per-package accounting), then a Tier-3 order-path change.
